decision.trend: Research has been focused on developing high-entropy alloys (HEAs) with enhanced properties such as strength, ductility, and corrosion resistance. Recent studies have explored the effects of processing techniques, such as spark plasma sintering, laser cladding, and high-pressure high-temperature treatment, on the microstructure and properties of HEAs. Additionally, the role of chemical composition, particularly the addition of elements like Cr, has been investigated to improve the oxidation resistance and corrosion properties of HEAs.
decision.unsolved: Despite the progress made, there is still a need to develop HEAs with balanced strength and ductility, as well as improved corrosion resistance and oxidation behavior. The strength-ductility trade-off remains a challenge, and further research is required to overcome this limitation.
decision.why: Based on the trend of research in HEAs, the next step would be to focus on microstructure architecture, specifically grain refinement and precipitation engineering, to achieve enhanced properties. This approach has shown promise in recent studies, such as the use of stationary friction processing to refine the grain size and improve the oxidation resistance of AlCoCrFeNi HEA. By controlling the microstructure and precipitation, it may be possible to overcome the strength-ductility trade-off and develop HEAs with improved corrosion resistance and oxidation behavior.
